1	// Shared hostname-uniqueness helpers for every place a `Server` row is
2	// created (VPS order, game order, NxCloud order, admin-granted free VPS,
3	// the e2e/seed script). Plain server module (not "use server").
4	//
5	// BACKGROUND: `Server.hostname` used to be a plain, unconstrained String.
6	// Every checkout path that left the field blank silently fell back to the
7	// exact same literal default ("web-01" for VPS), and nothing checked a
8	// customer-typed name for collision either — so the live DB ended up with
9	// several unrelated customers all named "web-01". A hostname-keyed lookup
10	// (scripts/recover-errored-server.mjs, working a "VPS web-01 stuck in ERROR"
11	// ticket) then had no way to tell those customers apart and grabbed the
12	// wrong one's row, surfacing a stranger's SSH port/status while working a
13	// different customer's ticket (2026-09-24 incident, hsw901013@gmail.com).
14	// `Server.hostname` is now `@unique` (prisma/schema.prisma) — this module is
15	// how every writer stays on the right side of that constraint instead of
16	// crashing checkout on the first collision.
17	import { db } from "./db";
18	// The pure, DB-free pieces (format/reservation rules, normalization, random
19	// suffixes, the P2002 sniff) live in ./hostname-shared, which has no server-
20	// only imports — so components/nx/order.tsx (a CLIENT component that pre-
21	// fills the checkout hostname field) can import them directly without pulling
22	// `./db` into the browser bundle. Re-exported below so every existing caller
23	// of "./hostname" keeps working exactly as before.
24	import {
25	  HOSTNAME_RE,
26	  HOSTNAME_MAX_LEN,
27	  RESERVED_HOSTNAMES,
28	  normalizeHostname,
29	  randHostnameSuffix,
30	  genDefaultVpsHostname,
31	  isHostnameConflict,
32	} from "./hostname-shared";
33	
34	export {
35	  HOSTNAME_RE,
36	  HOSTNAME_MAX_LEN,
37	  RESERVED_HOSTNAMES,
38	  normalizeHostname,
39	  randHostnameSuffix,
40	  genDefaultVpsHostname,
41	  isHostnameConflict,
42	};
43	
44	/** True when `hostname` (already normalized) is reserved or already belongs
45	 *  to another Server row. For a tool where the caller explicitly chose the
46	 *  name (an admin form, an ops script) and silently substituting a different
47	 *  one would be confusing, prefer this + a clear "pick another" error over
48	 *  resolveUniqueHostname's auto-suffix, which is for CUSTOMER checkout paths
49	 *  where blocking the purchase on a collision would be the worse outcome. */
50	export async function isHostnameTaken(hostname: string): Promise<boolean> {
51	  return RESERVED_HOSTNAMES.has(hostname) || !!(await db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname }, select: { id: true } }));
52	}
53	
54	/**
55	 * Resolve a customer-typed (or blank) hostname candidate into one that's
56	 * actually free right now, auto-suffixing on collision instead of failing
57	 * checkout or silently handing out a name someone else already has.
58	 * `fallbackPrefix` seeds the name when `rawCandidate` is blank — e.g. "web"
59	 * for a VPS, the game family for a game server.
60	 *
61	 * This is an ordinary precheck (`findFirst`), the same idiom
62	 * isSubdomainAvailable (lib/game-subdomain.ts) uses — good enough to catch
63	 * the common case (including the entire "everyone left it as web-01" class
64	 * of bug, which isn't timing-sensitive at all), but NOT itself race-proof
65	 * against two concurrent checkouts picking the exact same candidate in the
66	 * same instant. The `Server.hostname` unique constraint is the real,
67	 * final guard for that: callers must still wrap their `create` in a
68	 * try/catch and turn a residual `isHostnameConflict` into a clear "please
69	 * try again" error, exactly like changeGameSubdomain (lib/actions-server.ts)
70	 * already does for `Server.subdomain`.
71	 */
72	export async function resolveUniqueHostname(rawCandidate: string, fallbackPrefix: string): Promise<string> {
73	  let base = normalizeHostname(rawCandidate);
74	  if (!base) base = `${fallbackPrefix}-${randHostnameSuffix()}`;
75	  // Leave room for a "-xxxx" suffix (5 chars) without exceeding the 40-char
76	  // cap every checkout flow already enforces on the format.
77	  base = base.slice(0, HOSTNAME_MAX_LEN - 6) || fallbackPrefix.slice(0, HOSTNAME_MAX_LEN - 6);
78	
79	  let candidate = base;
80	  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 6; attempt++) {
81	    const taken =
82	      RESERVED_HOSTNAMES.has(candidate) ||
83	      !!(await db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: candidate }, select: { id: true } }));
84	    if (!taken) return candidate;
85	    candidate = `${base}-${randHostnameSuffix(4)}`;
86	  }
87	  // Last resort after 6 straight collisions (astronomically unlikely) — a
88	  // millisecond-timestamp tail that cannot repeat within this process.
89	  return `${base}-${Date.now().toString(36)}`;
90	}

       gp.name as gameplan_name, gp.\"priceCents\" as gameplan_price, gp.\"termMonths\" as gp_term,

left join \"Plan\" p on p.id = s.\"planId\"

15	 * already relies on (`description: { contains: server.hostname }`). This module
16	 * follows that same convention, scoped additionally by `userId` (a server's
17	 * hostname is unique to begin with, but scoping by owner removes any residual
18	 * cross-customer collision risk entirely).
19	 *
20	 * Primary source: Invoice, because it is the actual billing document (what the
21	 * customer sees on /dashboard/invoices, tax-inclusive) and — verified against
22	 * production data — has hostname coverage for every charge type: the initial
23	 * order (VPS AND game), renewals, upgrades, and every add-on (dedicated IP,
24	 * disk, backups). PAID invoices net their own `refundedCents` (an admin
25	 * partial/full refund via `refundPayment` updates the SAME invoice, never
26	 * creates a new one); a small number of cancellations issue a separate
27	 * "credit note" invoice with `status: "REFUNDED"` and a positive `amountCents`
28	 * (see `actions-server-lifecycle.ts`'s immediate-cancel refund) — those are
29	 * subtracted.
30	 *
31	 * Known, verified gap this module corrects for: a mid-term DOWNGRADE credit
32	 * (`actions-server-lifecycle.ts`, "Downgrade to … (prorated credit)") and a
33	 * job-failure refund (worker/index.ts, "Refund: failed …") both only touch
34	 * WalletTransaction — no Invoice is written or adjusted for either. Both are
35	 * folded in as corrections below so they are not silently missed. (A downgrade
36	 * credit that is later clawed back on a failed resize — "Reversed downgrade
37	 * credit …" — is included too, so the two net to zero exactly as they do in
38	 * the customer's real wallet balance.)
39	 *
40	 * Separately verified: the very first WalletTransaction line for a GAME
41	 * server order (lib/game-order.ts, `Game server: <plan> (<family>) — <term>`)
42	 * omits the hostname — unlike every sibling call site. It doesn't normally
43	 * matter here (Invoice is primary and DOES carry the hostname for that same
44	 * charge, since commit 5ecc6eedf4 "Create an Invoice + invoice-new email for
45	 * game-server orders", 2026-08-27) — but any game server ordered BEFORE that
46	 * commit has NO invoice at all, only that hostname-less WalletTransaction
47	 * debit, and would otherwise show $0 lifetime spend despite having genuinely
48	 * paid. Verified against production: exactly this happened to one live
49	 * customer server (terraria-i2ydef, ordered 2026-08-26). Recovered below via
50	 * a time-proximity fallback (same owner, a "Game server:" debit within 60s of
51	 * the server's own `createdAt` — the two rows are written in the same
52	 * transaction, so in practice they land within a couple of milliseconds of
53	 * each other) ONLY when no invoice at all matched this server's hostname, so
54	 * a normal (post-fix) order is never double-counted.
55	 */
56	export async function resolveServerLifetimeSpendCents(
57	  servers: { id: string; hostname: string; userId: string; createdAt: Date }[],
58	): Promise<Map<string, number>> {
59	  const result = new Map<string, number>();
60	  if (servers.length === 0) return result;
61	
62	  const userIds = Array.from(new Set(servers.map((s) => s.userId)));
63	
64	  const [invoices, corrections, preInvoiceGameOrders] = await Promise.all([
65	    db.invoice.findMany({
66	      where: { userId: { in: userIds }, status: { in: ["PAID", "REFUNDED"] } },
67	      select: { userId: true, description: true, amountCents: true, refundedCents: true, status: true },
68	    }),
69	    db.walletTransaction.findMany({
70	      where: {
71	        userId: { in: userIds },
72	        OR: [
73	          { description: { startsWith: "Downgrade to" } },
74	          { description: { startsWith: "Refund: failed" } },
75	          { description: { startsWith: "Reversed downgrade credit" } },
76	        ],
77	      },
78	      select: { userId: true, description: true, amountCents: true },
79	    }),
80	    // Fallback pool for the pre-5ecc6eedf4 (2026-08-27) gap documented above:
81	    // game-order debits that never got an invoice and don't carry a hostname.
82	    db.walletTransaction.findMany({
83	      where: { userId: { in: userIds }, description: { startsWith: "Game server:" }, amountCents: { lt: 0 } },
84	      select: { userId: true, amountCents: true, createdAt: true },
85	    }),
86	  ]);
87	
88	  for (const s of servers) {
89	    let cents = 0;
90	    let anyInvoiceMatched = false;
91	
92	    for (const inv of invoices) {
93	      if (inv.userId !== s.userId || !inv.description.includes(s.hostname)) continue;
94	      anyInvoiceMatched = true;
95	      if (inv.status === "PAID") {
96	        cents += inv.amountCents - (inv.refundedCents ?? 0);
97	      } else if (inv.status === "REFUNDED") {
98	        // A standalone credit-note invoice (e.g. "Cancellation refund — host")
99	        // — its amountCents is the positive amount returned to the customer.
100	        cents -= inv.amountCents;
101	      }
102	    }
103	
104	    for (const c of corrections) {
105	      if (c.userId !== s.userId || !c.description.includes(s.hostname)) continue;
106	      // amountCents > 0 (Downgrade credit, failed-job refund) reduces spend;
107	      // amountCents < 0 (a clawed-back downgrade credit) restores it.
108	      cents -= c.amountCents;
109	    }
110	
111	    if (!anyInvoiceMatched) {
112	      const fallback = preInvoiceGameOrders.find(
113	        (t) => t.userId === s.userId && Math.abs(t.createdAt.getTime() - s.createdAt.getTime()) <= 60_000,
114	      );
115	      if (fallback) cents += -fallback.amountCents;
116	    }
117	
118	    result.set(s.id, Math.max(0, cents));
119	  }
120	
121	  return result;
122	}

Fix hostname-rename spend blackout and direction-blind Grandfathered tag

Two more real bugs found on top of f304a18147, from the same 2026-09-25
fleet screenshot.

BUG A — Total Spent went blank ("—") for 6 servers. Root cause:
resolveServerLifetimeSpendCents (lib/server-spend.ts) and
regenerateMissingInvoices (lib/actions-billing.ts) both match a server's
real Invoice/WalletTransaction rows by substring-searching the server's
CURRENT hostname inside the record's description (there's no FK). A real
hostname-dedupe run on 2026-09-24 renamed 6 duplicate "web-01" servers to
unique names, so every invoice written before the rename still says
"web-01" and the substring match silently stopped finding them.

Added Server.previousHostnames (String[]) so a rename can never again
sever a record from the server that earned it: scripts/dedupe-hostnames.ts
now appends the old name on every rename, and both matching sites check
current-OR-any-previous hostname. scripts/backfill-previous-hostnames-
2026-09-24-dedupe.ts backfills the 6 already-renamed servers, sourced from
their own AuditLog "admin.hostname_dedupe" entries.

Verified read-only against production: all 6 currently show $0 lifetime
spend; simulating the fix against real invoice data restores $20.99 for
web-01-oyrj/web-01-pvm4 (single real order each) and $25.98 for the other
4 (which, because their owners briefly held two servers both literally
named "web-01" before the rename, sums both of that owner's orders — a
pre-existing description-matching ambiguity with no FK to fully resolve,
not introduced by this fix). The actual DB schema push + backfill against
production is BLOCKED by this environment's prod-deploy gate and still
needs to be run by the owner/operator once approved; the script is ready.

BUG B — the Grandfathered tag doesn't check direction. f304a18147 tagged
"Grandfathered" whenever the locked rate merely DIFFERED from live,
including when locked is HIGHER than live (the customer paying MORE than
a new customer today) — the owner flagged web-01-oyrj and
minecraft-qj4rxt exactly for this. serverFleetTags now only tags when the
locked rate is strictly LOWER than live (genuinely favorable). Updated
test/admin-fleet.test.ts's two divergence tests to be direction-aware and
added explicit "locked higher than live -> not tagged" cases for both the
VPS and game-server paths.

Investigated (read-only) whether renewalCharge (lib/renewal-charge.ts,
which has no direction check either) has ever actually billed a customer
the inflated locked rate: across the whole fleet, exactly 2 servers have
grandfatheredRenewalCents set above their live plan/game-plan price —
web-01-oyrj ($37.78 locked vs $30.22 live Pro) and minecraft-qj4rxt
($16.18 locked vs $12.94 live Minecraft 4GB/20). Both are legitimate: an
owner-requested 20% across-the-board renewal-price cut landed 2026-09-22
(AuditLog "plan.renewal_price.bulk_decrease"), AFTER both servers were
sold at the old regular price (3778*0.8=3022, 1618*0.8=1294 — exact
matches), so this is real price-drop-since-purchase, not bad data.
Neither server has reached its first renewal yet (both monthly, sold
2026-09-17 and 2026-09-20), and in fact NO server carrying any locked
rate, in either direction, has passed its expiresAt since the
grandfather program started 2026-09-17 — so the real-money impact of
renewalCharge's missing direction check is $0.00 to date. renewalCharge's
behavior and any live grandfatheredRenewalCents value are left untouched
pending the owner's decision on whether a stale locked-higher rate should
auto-correct down to live.

Typecheck clean. Full suite: 1459 pass / 40 fail, identical failing set
before and after this change (no regressions) — note this branch's actual
baseline is 40, not the 37 originally expected; flagging the discrepancy
rather than silently going with the stale number.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

content.text:
Both bugs are investigated, fixed, and verified against real production data on branch `fix/fleet-spend-rename-and-grandfathered-direction` in the isolated worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/fix-fleet-spend-and-grandfathered-direction` (commit `6bc4595112`, off current main `f304a18147`, nothing pushed or deployed).

**Bug A — Total Spent blank for 6 servers.** Confirmed the root cause exactly as summarized: `resolveServerLifetimeSpendCents` (`lib/server-spend.ts`) and `regenerateMissingInvoices` (`lib/actions-billing.ts`) both match invoices by substring-searching the server's *current* hostname, and the real 2026-09-24 dedupe run (verified via `AuditLog` `admin.hostname_dedupe` entries) renamed exactly these 6 servers from `web-01`: `cmu2olq84...→web-01-npto`, `cmu2p64ce...→web-01-q1uw`, `cmu3tci1r...→web-01-n6kl`, `cmu3uc3gw...→web-01-aelb`, `cmu5yv2gn...→web-01-oyrj`, `cmuevsfqn...→web-01-pvm4`. Added `Server.previousHostnames String[]` (`prisma/schema.prisma`), made `scripts/dedupe-hostnames.ts` append to it on every rename (it's the *only* place `Server.hostname` is ever changed after creation — I verified this by searching every `server.update` call site, not just the ones the task suggested), and updated both matching sites to check current-OR-any-previous hostname. Also updated the caller in `app/admin/servers/page.tsx` and a second real caller I found, `worker/index.ts`'s `archiveServerBeforeDelete`.

Wrote `scripts/backfill-previous-hostnames-2026-09-24-dedupe.ts` (dry-run by default, sourced verbatim from the real AuditLog rows) for the 6-server backfill. I could not actually run the prod schema push or the backfill — the Claude Code auto-mode classifier blocked it as a "Production Deploy" action, and I did not try to route around that. I instead proved the fix correct by simulating it in-memory against real prod invoice data: all 6 servers currently show **$0.00** lifetime spend; with the fix, `web-01-oyrj` and `web-01-pvm4` correctly restore to **$20.99** each (their one real invoice), and `web-01-npto`/`web-01-n6kl` and `web-01-q1uw`/`web-01-aelb` restore to **$25.98** each — worth flagging: those 4 are two owner-pairs (`intridaltd`, `want2bthereltd`) who each briefly held two servers *literally both named* "web-01" before the rename, so with no FK the substring match sums both of that owner's orders per server rather than splitting them individually ($12.99 each would be exact); this ambiguity pre-dates and is independent of my fix and isn't resolvable without a bigger schema change than what was asked. **The owner/operator still needs to run `npx prisma db push` then `npx tsx scripts/backfill-previous-hostnames-2026-09-24-dedupe.ts --apply` against prod** to actually restore this on the live site.

**Bug B — direction-blind Grandfathered tag.** Fixed `serverFleetTags` in `lib/admin-fleet.ts` to only tag when the locked rate is strictly *lower* than live; updated `test/admin-fleet.test.ts`'s two tests to be direction-aware and added explicit "locked-higher-than-live → not tagged" cases for both VPS and game-server paths (16/16 tests pass). For the real-money investigation: across the entire fleet, exactly two servers have a locked rate above live — `web-01-oyrj` (VM 130, locked $37.78 vs live $30.22 Pro) and `minecraft-qj4rxt` (VM 132, locked $16.18 vs live $12.94 Minecraft 4GB/20). Both are legitimate: the owner cut all renewal pricing 20% on 2026-09-22 (`AuditLog` `plan.renewal_price.bulk_decrease`), and both servers were sold just before that at the old regular price ($37.78×0.8=$30.22, $16.18×0.8=$12.94 — exact matches) — not stale/bad data. Critically, **no customer has actually been overcharged**: neither server has reached its first (monthly) renewal yet, and system-wide, zero servers carrying any locked rate (either direction) have passed their `expiresAt` since the grandfather program started 2026-09-17 — the real-money impact of `renewalCharge`'s missing direction check is **$0.00 to date**. I left `renewalCharge` and all live `grandfatheredRenewalCents` values untouched, per instructions, pending the owner's decision on whether stale locked-higher rates should auto-correct.

**Verification:** typecheck clean; full suite 1459 pass / 40 fail, identical failing set before and after (confirmed via git stash on the same commit) — note the actual baseline on `f304a18147` is 40, not the 37 the task described; flagging that discrepancy rather than silently adopting the stale number.

result: Both fleet-list bugs fixed and committed to branch `fix/fleet-spend-rename-and-grandfathered-direction` (`/tank/dev-worktrees/fix-fleet-spend-and-grandfathered-direction`, commit `6bc4595112`) with full real-data verification and a ready-to-run backfill script — the one remaining step, the actual prod DB schema push + backfill for the 6 renamed servers, is blocked by the environment's prod-deploy permission gate and needs the owner to run `npx prisma db push` then `scripts/backfill-previous-hostnames-2026-09-24-dedupe.ts --apply`; Bug B's real-money investigation found **zero dollars** have actually been overcharged so far.
